topology_reasoning.visual_evidence: Two separate strip-waveguide paths enter at a large vertical separation, use smooth mirrored S-bends to approach, remain parallel across a long interaction region, and fan back out. In the interaction region the upper guide narrows while the lower guide widens, with their combined width and edge-to-edge gap approximately constant. This is a counter-tapered adiabatic transfer section rather than a fixed-width directional coupler.
topology_reasoning.operating_principle: The close parallel section supports coupled local supermodes. Counter-tapering the two guide widths sweeps their propagation-constant mismatch through the transfer region, enabling adiabatic power transfer while the gap controls coupling strength.
topology_reasoning.planned_construction: Use only gf.Path centerlines extruded with custom width transitions, plus straight primitive leads. The two mirrored cosine-like S transitions will preserve horizontal tangency; the long interaction section will use linear counter-tapers. All material is placed on layer (1, 0).
